The protocol length l2 is not the captured buffer extent. strncmp can read tl1 bytes past snapend; ND_TTEST2 adds the missing capture-bound check. Diff header has a duplicated signature, but the local check and vulnerable expression are unambiguous.
The fallback loop intentionally relies on signed time_t a*2+1 overflowing to terminate. Signed overflow is undefined; the replacement derives the limit using unsigned bit operations.
OBJ_obj2txt returns required length, which can exceed the 128-byte output buffer. BIO_write trusts that length; switching to a terminated string bounds the actual read.

The demonstrated bug is unsigned-to-signed conversion of readU32, producing a negative len that bypasses the upper-bound check. The negative len+1 need not overflow. Exact CWE-190 is misleading; a conversion/negative-index label is more accurate.

At i equal to the fixed name limit, the original && evaluates id->name[i] before the bound and performs one out-of-bounds read. Swapping operands short-circuits it. No further iterations are needed for the defect.

For nonnegative representable lengths, data_size-header_size cannot overflow and the loop bound ensures memcmp has header_size remaining. The audit claims the opposite and supplies no reachable extreme signed-length precondition. Exclude as unproven.
last+1 can overflow signed int before pidmap indexing. The patch rejects out-of-range last and uses unsigned input, preventing the overflow and negative/out-of-range index path.

Header lengths are packed into fixed-width portions of info without checking their representable ranges; oversized name/value lengths spill into adjacent fields. The patch enforces those exact ranges before packing.
Parsing begins at *p+2 without checking serialized-buffer end. The added max-2 guard prevents a truncated input from reaching the numeric parser outside the buffer.

The minimum fixed-point coordinate sign-extends to 0xffff8000, so comparison to 0x8000 misses it. The subsequent subtraction overflows the lower representable bound; correcting the sentinel enables saturation.
Tile maximum addition occurs in narrow integer coordinates before the clamp, so overflow defeats the clamp. Int64 intermediates and comparisons prevent that local arithmetic overflow.

The signed int string counter can overflow while traversing a string longer than INT_MAX and then index incorrectly. size_t fixes the counter type. Do not rely on the audit claim of a mismatched malloc/memcpy size; both use the same expression.
size plus the allocation header can wrap size_t before ExAllocatePoolWithTag. RtlSizeTAdd rejects that overflow before allocation and the header store.
len+1 and alignment arithmetic can wrap into a small allocation size and evade the nsiz-only maximum check. The patch checks original len before allocation and uses unsigned size state.

The fragment-count/product is computed unchecked in unsigned int and can wrap before kmalloc. The fix introduces a division-based multiplication bound; its SIZE_MAX bound is architecture-dependent and should not be read as proving every 64-bit narrowing case safe.
An ASN.1 policy has an explicit length and need not end in NUL. The %s output reads past that buffer; the patch supplies precision from policy->length.
A very negative axis remains negative after one normalization, passes the upper-bound-only guard, and causes input_dims.data[-1] on i=0. The added lower-bound check fixes that read.

Fragment-count times iovec size is unchecked before g_malloc; it can wrap on size_t-limited builds. g_new performs overflow-checked multiplication. The separate count addition may need its own bound but does not negate the demonstrated product flaw.

The 32-bit serviceId read crosses a 16-bit field boundary, but the existing guard reserves the whole header plus four opcode bytes. The supplied evidence does not show a read beyond the captured buffer; this change can simply correct field decoding. The audit overread explanation is inconsistent with the guard.

A cursor *begin already beyond strlen(str) is dereferenced before validation. The added initial bound check repairs that local read. The audit is wrong that isspace/isalnum continue through NUL; those redundant loop checks are not the proof.

Length-delimited ASN.1 email data reaches C-string duplicate comparison and strdup without guaranteed termination. Bounded duplication followed by comparison of the terminated copy fixes those overreads.
The display-copy branch bypasses BLTUNSAFE while the fallback checks it. Moving validation before the branch protects both blit paths from out-of-range video-memory coordinates.
The precondition allows next_byte_index == nb_bytes. If end_of_input is not yet set, the subsequent in_buf read is one past the buffer. The added bytes-left test closes that state.

The demonstrated local flaw is narrowing int64_t size to the int argument of av_new_packet, not arithmetic wrap in this function. CWE-197/conversion or the resulting write class is more precise than the claimed CWE-190.
A 0-3-byte vector is read as a U32 before checking its size. The added size>=4 condition protects the magic-number read.
The output has rank-1 slots, but an invalid axis skips no input dimension and writes rank values. Explicit lower/upper axis checks make exactly one dimension omitted.
The allocation multiplies untrusted vector count by context size without checking overflow. Replacing kzalloc(product) with kcalloc(count,size) adds overflow-checked allocation.
Repeated extension-length additions can wrap the u16 cursor and defeat the loop bound. Widening it and rejecting sums at IPV6_MAXPLEN prevents the wraparound.
Four unrestricted signed decimal integers can format beyond a 16-byte IPv4 buffer before inet_aton validates the string. Bounded snprintf repairs the direct stack write.

The added recursive is_valid_filename resolves symlink ancestors before accepting. This is a verified directory escape within broader CWE-22, with CWE-59 as the more specific mechanism.

Inspected this extractor and its sanitizer sibling plus the complete upstream patch. The pre-fix sanitizer only checks lexical containment, allowing archive-created symlink parents to escape the destination, and this function writes those returned paths. The patched sanitizer resolves ancestors and returns NULL; this caller then skips rejected entries. CWE-22 describes the verified directory escape, with a symlink-following mechanism.

Inspected upstream parser source including next_state_val and TK_CC_RANGE. next_state_class changes CCS_START to CCS_VALUE without establishing vs; a following range consumes that endpoint in the mixed-type bitset_set_range path. Preserving CCS_START prevents the uninitialized range index and resulting out-of-bounds bitset write.

Verified downstream lha_read_data_none in upstream source: negative compsize becomes entry_bytes_remaining, replaces positive bytes_avail with a negative value, and is passed to lha_crc16/buffer size reporting. The missing post-subtraction negative-size rejection therefore causes an over-read, not just an arithmetic anomaly.

Verified http2_handle_stream_close consumer: it reads each uint32 length then advances by n+1 without a remaining-size check. The producer undercounts ': ' plus CRLF by one, leaving the cursor at the prior terminator; the next length read can pass the buffer end or form a bogus huge payload read. Fixing +3 to +4 restores record boundaries.

The non-long-salt branch constructs eight-byte padding plus input digest plus salt directly in pkcsBlock, while the existing bound covers hLen+saltLen+2 only. Thus valid final encoded-message dimensions can still overrun this temporary construction. The fix allocates a separate correctly sized message buffer when necessary.

The concrete changed expression reads source_p[0] before checking source_p==source_end_p. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), not the supplied CWE-787 write label. Automated audit calls the read real but fails to reject the wrong label.

Attacker-controlled CU length establishes pu_pub_entries_end_ptr beyond the actual section and is supplied as the bound to string validation before strlen. The added explicit length and end-pointer checks prevent string scans beyond the mapped section. This caller creates the invalid bound for the described helper over-read.

Verified pinned OpenSMTPD parse.y, mda_variables.c, smtpd.h and mda_unpriv.c. Nonempty invalid localpart with empty domain bypasses validation and returns success. The mbox command interpolates mbox.from without quotes and execle invokes /bin/sh -c; MAILADDR_ESCAPE omits semicolon and double quote. Thus the missing localpart check permits actual downstream shell syntax, establishing CWE-78 despite the sanitizer-only local function.

Thin wrapper only calls reference_ops::GatherNd and returns success; no bounds calculation or read is visible, and its patch merely propagates a newly introduced helper status. Insufficient function-local evidence to use this as a distinct labeled memory-read sample.

Thin wrapper only calls reference_ops::ScatterNd and returns success. The changed return propagation does not itself add write bounds checking, which lives entirely in the helper. Excluded as an insufficiently self-contained labeled memory-write sample.

Diff conditionally omits formatting quotes; all output appends use a managed builder and no concrete overflowing destination or changed bounds are established. This does not substantiate the supplied CWE-787 flaw.

Supplied CVE description names a different packet iterator; patch substitutes the loop-local component pointer in a shift guard. Insufficient evidence that this particular change is the claimed buffer over-read rather than stale-pointer/check logic.

Verified pinned image_loader_tga.h declares image_width and image_height uint16_t. Both promote to signed int before multiplication, so 65535*65535 overflows before later size_t multiplication. The automated claim that final size_t prevents this is incorrect. The supplied patch improves downstream read bounds but does not fully fix this pre-existing CWE-190 arithmetic defect.

Recovered intact do_ed_script from the pinned upstream parent, retaining the complete fork/error/cleanup branches. sprintf inserts outname unquoted in buf and execl invokes /bin/sh -c buf. The fix directly executes the editor with separate arguments. This restores source integrity but requires fresh recall evidence under the new ID.

Verified pinned ecma-globals.h defines ENTRY_COUNT as item_count-1, the GC map marker iterates pairs and reads entry_p->value, and collection_push_back reallocates when capacity is full. If the key fills the final slot, GC during the second append sees an odd pair count and reads the value slot beyond capacity. The pair append fix reserves both slots together. CWE-125 is supported; the automated claim that this must instead be use-after-free is not justified.
Duration reconciliation in get_over does not establish the described calculate_beam buffer-read defect in this function. Excluded for insufficient local mechanism/fix evidence.

Original paired diff is a different Sparse/Ragged kernel. Recovered actual upstream patch changes shape validation but does not fix the visible missing negative-batch check. Cannot reliably align this record, supplied CVE and fix mechanism without a new corrected description and rejudging.
The 32-to-128 byte output buffer change concerns a potential formatted-time write overflow, not supplied CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. Requires relabeling and fresh judged recall.

The precise defect is size_t subtraction below zero for a sub-block remainder, CWE-191 integer underflow. It is not the supplied CWE-190 increasing-value overflow and cannot keep that ground-truth label.

The security-relevant added guard prevents size minus four becoming a huge unsigned memcpy length. This is CWE-191 underflow, not the supplied CWE-190 label; unchanged accumulation is insufficient evidence for the stated CVE mechanism.

Missing boolean stack entry causes stack-state inconsistency consumed in another handler. Local attribute reads are paired under parser invariants; this function does not substantiate the supplied CWE-125 mechanism. Also the displayed fix uses a different zval layout, so paired evidence is unreliable.

utf2char advances the destination for every UTF-16 unit with no destination capacity argument or check. The fix introduces bufsz and reserves a terminator byte, directly bounding the previously unchecked writes.

SMP Encryption Information handler copies sixteen bytes from peer packet data without validating parameters or available payload. The fix rejects invalid parameters before STREAM_TO_ARRAY, preventing the truncated-packet source over-read.
SanityCheck evaluates actions[n-1] even when the CALLFUNCTION action is the first action (n=0). The fix short-circuits with n>0 before that negative-index read.

The bounds mismatch permits bfd_get_64 to READ eight bytes after validating offset_size, potentially four. This is CWE-125, not the assigned CWE-787 write label; the audit describes the read but accepts the wrong label.

The file-position delta can be zero in the malformed/empty-line case but is immediately used as length-1 to read linebuff. The added positive-length guard prevents the negative-index access; the existing CR guard demonstrates the same required condition.

EOF flushing subtracts eight until cur_bits is nonpositive, potentially negative. A later output call indexes masks[cur_bits] before any check. The fix marks completion and returns on re-entry, preventing that negative-index read.

The capture check covers ip6f_offlg but the verbose branch also reads the later four-byte ip6f_ident. A truncated fragment header can therefore pass the check and over-read. The fix validates the complete fragment header.

An arbitrarily long URI passing the depth test is memcpy'd after the static prefix into path[128]. No length check limits that write. The fix checks prefix length plus URI length against the destination capacity before copying.

GetByte unconditionally reads an input byte. The specific flaw is CWE-125 over-read, not CWE-787 write. Reject the automated assertion that the read/write distinction is minor for exact ground-truth labels.

thread_call pushes a root table and caller-counted parameters onto the target VM stack without reserving space. The fix reserves nparams+3 before these writes, directly addressing target heap-stack capacity.

The handler reads two-byte EDIV plus eight-byte random data from an unchecked SMP packet. The fix requires eleven total bytes including the opcode before reading, preventing truncated-packet over-read.

The faulty ppos and snprintf length handling exposes an out-of-bounds source read. Although ignoring count also violates the read destination contract, the supplied CWE-787 kernel-memory write mechanism is not established. The audit wrongly treats read and write labels as interchangeable.

Only new keycode is range-checked. An oversized old_keycode makes is_event_supported false; its negation therefore permits __test_and_clear_bit on an out-of-range bit index into dev->key. The fix explicitly checks old_keycode against KEY_MAX before this read-modify-write.

Only initial AIGP length is checked for three bytes. A preceding TLV can leave one or two bytes; while(length) then reads the next two-byte length before validating availability. The fix checks remaining bytes before ptr_get_be16.

For adjusted route-target prefix lengths below four bytes, the existing capture check does not cover EXTRACT_32BITS(pptr+1). The fix separately validates the four-byte origin AS and corrects the route-target offset to pptr+5.

The line-ending search increments end until newline without checking fulltext.size(). A final line without newline passes the permitted terminator position and then reads beyond the string. The fix bounds the loop by size; acceptance does not rely on falsely treating operator[size()] alone as invalid.

Guest vertex_buffer_index is loaded without a bound and stored in vertex-element state for later fixed-size buffer indexing. The fix rejects values >=PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS at ingestion, matching the described draw-stage over-read.

The sfsname branch copies a fixed NFSX_V3FHMAX bytes from a packet-derived file-handle string even when actual len is shorter and lacks a NUL. The fix caps strncpy by the actual handle length and terminates at that bound.

Packet size is trusted to construct a child buffer view using returned data and size without checking remaining tvb bytes. The upstream boundary check rejects an oversized declared length before creating that view, preventing downstream reads using the overstated extent.

The CWE-125 off-by-one is real, but this is the same function body as megavul_3d16dbb8f79e with its return/storage declaration missing. Retain the intact MegaVul version rather than count these as independent samples.

tlen includes the OID length byte, but safeputs starts at tptr+1 and reads oid_len bytes. The old check tlen>=oid_len is one short; the fix requires 1+oid_len. This intact function replaces duplicate PrimeVul extraction primevul_2553.

The displayed function is truncated after the loop and lacks the final function closing/return tail. Its offset-zero decrement is a real write bug, but source integrity must be recovered and rescanned before acceptance.

After advancing p by hdrlen, this function passes the original h containing unadjusted caplen/len to the nested printer. The resulting pointer/length mismatch authorizes reads beyond the payload. The fix supplies a copied header with both lengths reduced.
The late/off-by-one check permits reading sample_info[sampleCount], while writes to trun entries are separately indexed within nb_samples. This substantiates CWE-125, not supplied CWE-787.

The extraction is visibly truncated: allocation is followed by an orphaned if(i>0) body without its loop and the rest of cloop_open. The arithmetic flaw is plausible but malformed source cannot qualify without recovery and fresh scans.

The local end-tag bounds flaw is real, but the supplied description specifically names xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal, a different routine/mechanism. Consistent with rejected PrimeVul sibling: correct the description and rejudge before use.

The post-label check casts before adding one, testing only one byte from the label start, while the dereference adds one whole MPLS struct. If the final label ends at end_ptr, the next-byte read is outside the packet. The corrected check covers that exact byte.

CCS_VALUE writes BITSET_SET_BIT with an unchecked single-byte-class value. An octal token above 255 produces an index beyond the byte-class bitset; the fix adds the >0xff rejection already present in the range branch.

len starts at nonzero L2 offset but len_remaining starts at full datalen, overstating available MPLS bytes by that offset. The fix checks absolute read endpoints against pktdata+datalen. Its first-nibble fix remains incomplete, as documented in the separate later-fix sample.

Unmasked fast-path copies rely on a MAX_LZ_MATCH margin, but increased match lengths can exceed it near the window end. The fix uses MAX_INC_LZ_MATCH for both source and destination margin, routing those cases through masked copying and preventing heap writes beyond Window.

Only four-byte subtype presence is initially checked. The MTU branch reads two bytes at offset four without its own six-byte minimum, unlike the other branches. The added tlv_len<6 check prevents over-read.

A trailing escape or unfinished character class can advance p to end in an inner step and then again in the outer loop. The error formatting length includes that extra byte, causing an over-read. The fix jumps to failed immediately upon reaching end, preventing the extra increment; p==end alone is not the erroneous read length.

The per-skb stats flag fix establishes inappropriate data export, but proving a physical over-read needs the skb linear/nonlinear backing-length path, which is absent here. Excluded under the precise CWE-125 evidence requirement rather than assuming every inappropriate export is an out-of-bounds read.

A short SOFn segment can pass pos+length checks while the called SOFn parser requires eight bytes. The added length>=8 and remaining-eight-byte checks align the supplied pointer with the helper's fixed reads.
The 14-byte file header can contain v followed by four nonterminated digits. atoi(id+10) then scans beyond the stack array. The fix requires id[13] to be NUL before numeric parsing.

When the marker loop reads a non-FF last byte, its body length check is skipped and pos reaches the buffer end. php_jpg_get16 then reads out of bounds before subsequent length validation. The added pos<size check addresses this path, though a complete two-byte guard would be stronger.

Mask endpoints can exceed glyph->num_points after endchar reduces the point count. Unclamped first/next produce an out-of-range point span for hint mutation. The fix clamps both endpoints to the actual point array size.

After the NTLM message header, NegotiateFlags is read as four bytes without checking remaining input. The fix adds a four-byte remaining-length check before Stream_Read_UINT32, preventing a truncated-token over-read.

Inspected the full function: the UTF-32 output path can increment out to MAXSTRING without returning. A following ASCII iteration writes result->chars[out++] before its check. Moving the check before that write prevents the overflow; all-ASCII input alone does not demonstrate it.
The QoS mesh branch calls extract_mesh_header_length(p+hdrlen) before the later caplen<hdrlen check. The fix requires hdrlen+1 captured bytes before reading the Mesh Flags byte.

After consuming the final argument, i is incremented to NCH(n), then CHILD(n,i) is accessed for a possible comma without rechecking. The patch adds that child-count check before TYPE, preventing a one-past-end read.

The cache allocates/copies pkthdr->len bytes from pcap_next data, whose actual capture extent is caplen and may be shorter. This is a source over-read despite a sufficiently large destination. The patch routes reads through the safe packet helper.

Source advancement and weighted dereferences depend only on coverage arithmetic, with no source-row endpoint even for leftover contributions. The fix introduces src_limit and checks it at all dereferences/advance loops, preventing rounding-driven row over-read.

pr_str_get_word consumes raw quote/escape bytes but returns a shorter decoded word. Subtracting strlen(wrd) from buflen overstates bytes remaining after advanced ptr, so the CRNUL scan reads beyond input. Ignoring quote semantics for the command word removes this length mismatch.

The last-xattr search advances by entry-controlled sizes until a sentinel without checking the loaded buffer end. Malformed last entries drive subsequent header/sentinel reads outside that buffer. The patch bounds entry header and next-entry address against last_base_addr.

For a nonempty line, pos->col can exceed its length; posptr is then passed to multibyte head-offset inspection beyond the line. The fix clamps the column at the first NUL before forming/inspecting that pointer.

count is required to equal device report_size, but report_size need not be eight. Allocating eight then copy_from_user(count) causes a heap write overflow for longer reports. The fix allocates the actual count.

File bytes are read into malloc(length+1) without initializing a terminator; later C-string consumption can scan past the allocation. The fix requires NUL within the read data before using the creator string.

The claimed post-end loop read is blocked by enforce(sizeof(header)<=length-count) when count==length. Earlier subBox.length<=length-count prevents count exceeding length. The automated underflow narrative does not establish reachability; reject rather than infer an unshown different bug.

With dataLen zero, endPtr=dataPtr-1 is dereferenced during padding removal; computed negative unpadded length can also reach digest reading. The added dataLen>0 guard prevents this pre-buffer read path.

memchr starts at pos+1 but its length is filename_len-offset+1, two bytes larger than the actual remainder filename_len-offset-1. The patch corrects that subtraction, preventing extension search beyond filename bytes.

Matching an ASF stream GUID does not ensure the fixed stream flags at offset 72 have two available bytes. The fix requires 74 remaining bytes before AV_RL16; earlier chunk validation is insufficient for that fixed-offset read.
The IPv6 subnet ID branch requires only twenty bytes yet reads sixteen address bytes plus sixteen mask bytes. Raising the minimum to thirty-two prevents accesses beyond short identity data.
The command-name scan follows printable bytes without an end pointer, so unterminated ELF note contents read past nbuf+size. The added cp<nbuf+size guard directly bounds the scan.

Capture checks use attacker-controlled cap_len, but multiprotocol capability decoding unconditionally reads through opt[i+5]. Short declared/captured payloads reach an out-of-bounds SAFI read. The fix checks that final byte explicitly.

SOS length is read from input independently of the computed fragment extent. memcpy writes length bytes into an allocation based on end-start plus fixed padding; sufficiently oversized length overflows it. The fix rejects length>end-start before allocation/copy.
After TLV header subtraction, magic-number decoding still reads four bytes regardless of remaining ie_len. The fix requires an exact four-byte payload before EXTRACT_32BITS.

TIM parsing already advances offset past the three fixed bytes, then adds another three to memcpy source. This reads three bytes past the validated element extent. Removing the duplicate offset corrects the source bound.

The TIM bitmap source uses attacker-controlled tim.length-3 relative to packet base instead of the current offset, so its copy can extend beyond captured bytes. The upstream change repairs that source-coordinate error but retains an extra three-byte offset, corrected by the later CVE-2017-13008 sample; the pre-fix over-read remains real.
The changed USHORT(bytes,1) reads past a two-byte input; no destination write overflow is established by this diff. Supplied CWE-787 must be corrected to CWE-125 and rejudged.

A zero-length BW_CONSTRAINTS subTLV passes the general zero-byte capture check but unconditionally dereferences *tptr for its model ID. The patch exits on subl==0 before that read and avoids unsigned subl-1 loop expansion.

Repeated alloca in an error loop exhausts the stack, but the local allocated buffer writes remain within outlen+256. This is unbounded stack/resource allocation rather than a demonstrated CWE-787 buffer write beyond its allocation.

Untrusted uint64 l participates in addition for the remaining-length guard and allocation before any upper bound. Wraparound makes those computed sizes small while subsequent operations retain l. The fix caps l at DATA_SIZE_MAX before arithmetic, directly addressing CWE-190 in journal field parsing.

Error dispatch increments osp then stores an error object without checking operand-stack end. The fix checks the incremented pointer against ostop before writing, preventing a full-stack out-of-bounds ref store.

WebP payload allocation uses chunk size but fixed-offset dimension copies require 10 bytes for VP8/VP8X, 5 for VP8L and 12 for ANMF. Only an upper file-size bound existed. The fix adds the missing per-format minimum sizes before reads.

Inspected decoder state loading and after_loop state saving: error_code returns before the normal persisted state update, despite intervening code-table mutations. Retrying resumes with inconsistent saved dictionary state and can follow invalid code pointers. The fix latches read_error and rejects re-entry after the bad-code path.

The Trailer-comment loop increments ioBuf.ptr until newline without checking ioBuf.limit. An unterminated comment therefore reads past the IO buffer. The patch adds the missing endpoint test directly to that loop.

A leading NUL in successful fgets makes strlen(readbuf) zero, so the newline-strip expression reads at index SIZE_MAX/before the buffer. This clearly supports CWE-125. The supplied conversion to getline retains the same faulty subtraction and is not a complete fix; retained as incomplete-fix evidence, not claimed remedied.

An oversized ckSize is used both to read into the fixed ds64_chunk stack object and to copy that object out via WavpackAddWrapper. The latter is an explicit over-read of the stack object, supporting CWE-125 alongside a secondary write overflow. The fix bounds both operations by sizeof(DS64Chunk).

The original length check compares total_length to the whole section while line_ptr starts at nonzero line_offset, creating an end bound beyond the section. Read helpers can then over-read. The patch incorporates line_offset in the bound; acceptance concerns the pre-fix mismatch.

Option capture validation covers only declared olen, yet HOLDTIME, GENID and REFRESH_CAP read fixed two/four-byte fields even for shorter options. The patch enforces each required option size before those reads.

Organization TLVs require only OUI/subtype before the Avaya branches consume a 32-byte digest and further fields. The added 50/36-byte minimum checks prevent short TLVs reaching those unconditional reads and the mapping-count subtraction.

moduleNameStr starts as an eight-byte strdup of Unknown, then unbounded sscanf scans a GSDML module value into it. The fix allocates MAX_NAMELENGTH and limits the scan to 199 characters, preventing the heap overwrite.

si_overrun accumulates it_overrun_last without saturation, allowing a large timer overrun count to overflow the user-visible integer. The fix replaces addition with timer_overrun_to_int and widens internal accounting, supporting the arithmetic-overflow label.

Signed int width*height is evaluated before size_t pixel-size multiplication in malloc; large cursor dimensions overflow and produce undersized allocation. The fix rejects negative and over-maximum dimensions before multiplication.

readRawProfile advances sp from byte one until newline without checking text.size_, so newline-free profile data runs off the heap buffer. The added position limit targets this over-read; very short inputs still merit separate fix-completeness scrutiny.

The no-padding DataOffset branch skips the only offset+length versus request-size check, then ksmbd_vfs_write reads that many source bytes. The fix applies the bound uniformly before selecting the data pointer.

The faulty section record bounds permit r_read_ble source over-reads. No CWE-787 write overflow is established by the changed guard; the supplied description itself says read, so the source label requires correction.

POSIX wordexp is invoked with flags zero on an externally supplied asset filepath. Double quotes do not disable command substitution; WRDE_NOCMD is absent. The fix returns the literal path without expansion. This verifies a specific CWE-78 refinement of source CWE-77.

Verified caller do_command reads fname separately from configured transfer command and passes both to run_cmd. This function concatenates that filename verbatim into a string executed by /bin/sh -c. The fix constructs argv and execvp, so the source CWE-77 can be specifically refined to OS command injection CWE-78.

Read this caller with the complete run_cmd sibling: read_filename data is appended to the configured send/receive command and executed by /bin/sh without quoting. The patch changes run_cmd to argv execution; this caller participates in that verified filename command-injection path.

Inspected pinned delegate-private.h: non-Windows SanitizeDelegateString explicitly allows semicolon, dollar, backtick, pipe and spaces. WriteVIDEOImage inserts that result unquoted after -pix_fmt and passes the constructed command to ExternalDelegateCommand. The fix single-quotes the sanitized option, preventing shell interpretation. Verified CWE-77 to CWE-78 refinement.

Verified the upstream sanitizer retains shell metacharacters. ReadVIDEOImage inserts sanitized video:vsync and video:pixel-format values unquoted into the command passed to ExternalDelegateCommand. The patch single-quotes each option on POSIX. This is OS shell injection rather than only additional-argument injection.

The loop requires only an option header, subtracts the declared total option size, then may memcpy an RFC structure even when len has become negative. olen matching sizeof(rfc) does not prove packet availability. The new negative-remainder check stops before that source copy.

Negotiation updates server->ops for SMB21/SMB311 while leaving server->vals at the default dialect. This produces the described mismatched packet layout/size interpretation. The fix updates both tables together in each negotiated-dialect branch, directly resolving the CVE's inconsistent parsing state.

parse_file_info trusts the directory's declared dr_len to bound later field/name/system-use reads without knowing available bytes. The fix adds reclen and rejects declared lengths beyond it, closing the crafted short-record over-read.

Inspected header-mask computation and fixed 256-byte red/green/blue maps: a 9-bit contiguous mask yields max=511 and the <= loop writes through index 511. The patch rejects oversized map maxima before the loops. Direct CWE-787.

Inspected complete function and diff. HTTP query name is concatenated under dir and opened for writing with request body; ../ components escape dir. The patch adds remove_double_dots before fopen. Refine original CWE-552 to the directly visible CWE-22 mechanism; fresh gate required.

Inspected full function and diff. Custom command ! prefix bypasses named-command lookup; remaining name is concatenated under AR_BINDIR without rejecting parent components.
